results.title: A must-see in Kathmandu
results.text: Definitely a must-see while in Kathmandu. The place has a very special spirit. Take a guide with you to understand the Hindu rituals!

results.title: Must visit when in Kathmandu
results.text: Not sure how you rate a temple. All I can say is do visit if in Kathmandu. Serene environment. Keep in mind clicking pictures inside the temple area is not allowed

results.title: Fascinating, interesting sight
results.text: First it looked like not much worth for the 1000 rupees of entrance fee - but when you walk around, there's actually a lot to see. The cremation of bodies by the river is, of course, very interesting and when a climb up the big stairs, there are a lot of temples up on the hill. This is definitely one of the most the most interesting sights in Kathmandu.

results.title: Gateway to heaven.
results.text: Located north east at the bank of Bagmati river in kathmandu. Pashupati nath  mean lord of beast, this place is very much popular for cremation in puplic. Every day many death people  are brought by family for final rituals in human life that is performed with great honored. Only hindus are allowed to enter the temple  but other can have good time walking around and watching cremation. Beautiful place to learn lot about life.

results.title: Place of peace
results.text: I would recommend this place to see not only a temple but some of the local traditions too. Popular with locals too

results.title: Interesting place but very crowded
results.text: It is a beautiful place to visit and my guide told me that this is the most sacred Hindu temple in the world. I loved the surroundings but the place was very dirty and crowded. Why do not the government clean and properly manages the place?

results.title: LORD SHIVA TEMPLE
results.text:
Only Hindus can enter the temple, temple is historical and very old. this place is very crowded.

The cremation area is just behind the temple and its doorstep to enter heaven as per Hindu believe.

results.title: Not to be missed when in Kathmandu!
results.text: Pashupatinath Temple is one of the holiest Hindu temples in the world. I was very fortunate to spend time there with a Nepalese friend who explained how, in the past, the while building by the river was to house those who were near death. It was like a hospice with doctors and caretakers. As the person came close to taking their last breath they are wrapped in cloth and taken to the river where their feet are washed (the river flows eventually into the holy Ganges River in india) while family/friends chant until they pass. The Hindu belief is that how we leave this life is how we enter the next, so they want the person to leave with only peace and thoughts of God. Today people are sent to hospitals and so do not come for this until they have died. After this ritual the body is cremated. There were many cremations going on while I was there. if you have time, it is a beautiful place to sit, observe and contemplate how spirit moving into the body, living in the body and leaving the body are all natural phases of life to be embraced. We were there in late afternoon and for the beginning of sunset. I am not certain about this, but I believe it is the best time to view the cremations.

results.title: Only Hindus allowed inside the main temple; quite polluted river near the cremation area.
results.text:
Being a Hindu, I was quite skeptical visiting yet another temple, not expecting it to be much different from the ones I had seen back home. But the architecture is quite different, for similar to Tibetan/East Asian style pagodas. 

There are many hawkers selling ceremonial-peripherals and souvenir items on the way to the temple. Once at the temple, you will be asked (if you are a Hindu) to remove your footwear and place it in a temple bag that will be kept safely in a shoe rack and a token for the same handed over to you. All non-Hindus can walk right up to the entrance of the gate and Hindus can proceed inside. There were idols of various deities inside and the prominent sight here that everyone on Trip Advisor seemed to be raving about was not quite pleasant/interesting (in my humble opinion) to watch. The river where the cremations were taking place was quite polluted and it was sad to see that nobody cared to clean it up.

results.title: Moving experience seeing Hindu culture!
results.text: This place is truly spiritual.  Seeing the shrines and cremation spots was unlike anything I have ever seen before ... certainly different for  westerners to see.  The way the local people deal with death is truly fascinating and I would encourage people to get a guide who will explain the meaning of certain functions in the cremation procedure and how relatives grieve for their loved ones.  My guide talked me through the steps involved in the process and I was lucky to witness actual cremations taking place.  It was truly moving.

results.title: One of the Most Unique Site I have Visited
results.text:
This is a place where people bring the dead for cremation.  The process is actually quite interesting and unlike anything I have ever visited before.  It is outdoors.  Out of respect for the dead, we decided not to take photos.

Entrance is 1000 rupees.  There is a temple where only Hindus can enter.  We spent about an hour here.

results.title: Unplanned visit
results.text: I had been here on a previous visit to Nepal, however I accompanied a friend and although I find it quite an oppressive place I also find it quite calm. We had a guide that befriended us at the entrance and this was worth the few hundred rupees we paid at the end to learn about the temples, steer us away from the monkies and protect us to some extent from the hawkers and beggars. Always be aware of your surroundings if visiting here

results.title: Blissful!
results.text:
The visit to Pashupatinath temple always brings in me a very blissful and tranquil experience. This is one one the most ancient and sacred Hindu temples in the world, a UNESCO heritage and is especially very crowded on Mondays and certain days in a month per lunar calendar. Only Hindus are permitted in the actual temple premises, however, there is a lot of fascinating and mysterious culture to explore beyond the actual temple premises. The temple lies on the banks of holy Bagmati river (like the Ganges in India) where the many Hindu rituals including cremations take place. Sights of sadhus dressed in colorful yellow and orange robes with ashes and long hair and beard, signs of worldly renunciation are common in the temple area; there are also a number of ashrams and 'bhajans' singing groups of people along with numerous temples and shrines in the area that adds a sense of spirituality in the region.

The view of the temple, flocks of people paying homage in the temple, the sadhus, the rituals, the river Bagmati, the architecture of the main temple and other temples - all of these add bliss to the environment. The view is most fascinating from the east side of the temple across the Bagmati river, where there are places for people to rest and experience the beautiful ambiance.

results.title: Cultural Experience
results.text: This is another UNESCO world heritage site, a must visit place when in nepal for cultural experience. You get to experience and learn about the traditions and religion. Wittness live the processions and ceremony.

results.title: The temple is viewable from a distance
results.text: Pashupatinath is the cremation area and temple along the river Bhagmati. Although you can't walk through it as you can in Varanasi, you can observe the cremations more easily from the bridges over the river. The temple is viewable from a distance although you can only enter if you're Hindu. Taxi rates are about three times higher in Katmandu than they were when I was here two years ago, so visits have to be better coordinated. Entry fee here is about $15.

results.title: A worthwhile visit
results.text: A must see on your list of places to see around Kathmandu.  Have a great time walking around and taking in all there is to see.

results.title: Breathing in former-human smoke
results.text:
It may sound morbid to anyone who hasn't yet been there, but it is strangely meditative and calming sitting on the bank of a low dirty river watching human bodies go up in flames.

Be sure to set aside at least a good half day to explore and absorb Pashupatinath. Follow the staircase that leads up from the east bank of the river to find some of Kathmandu's best relaxing trees and a good view of the city, watch out for monkeys (I have a friend who got randomly attacked), and walk around the old city part too. Can be linked with a walk to Boudnath.

Would give 5 stars, but the 1000 rupee entry fee is a little embitteringly steep, especially if you're spending a while in Kathmandu and end up having to pay it several times.

results.title: lord of all living pashupatinath
results.text:
various legend exist about the temple and origins but visiting this really old temple which is one of the important temples / place of worship for Hindus.
it has a ghat (cremation and prayer area for the departed, with a part reserved for royalty)
one can see people from all over the country and India offering prayers.

results.title: Favourite Temple
results.text: Of all the temples we visited this was by far the best. The entrance fee is high at 1000 Rps but there is so much to see it's worth it. Once inside we also hired a guide which was a good idea as he explained all the gods and temples really well. His name was Diamond (like the stone). We were told all about the cremation ceremony's and it was the best cultural experience we had during our trip. There are also lots of monkeys to see.
